headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from MemMachine MCP outputs feeding a writable, networked transformers pipeline.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, so its outputs can bridge into transformers workflows. Transformers can read files and run browsers, making it plausible that untrusted MemMachine content is consumed as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, but a direct shared channel is not proven, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF MemMachine output is copied into prompts or MCP messages consumed by transformers
IF transformers parses file or browser content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all MemMachine outputs before passing them onward
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported content
Require a human review step for any MemMachine-generated text
Restrict transformers to read-only inputs for one test run
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while transformers has broad filesystem read/write and network egress. If shared files or prompts carry those data classes into transformers, leakage can occur in default workflows. No direct evidence of a shared workspace is provided, so this is inferred rather than confirmed.
conditions: IF MemMachine context is written to a filesystem location readable by transformers
IF transformers sends imported text or files to a remote backend or hub
mitigations: Keep MemMachine context out of shared directories
Redact long-term user facts before handoff
Run transformers with network egress blocked for a quick test
Separate credentials and working folders per agent
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the handoff boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Transformers can write the filesystem, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses, while MemMachine can reach the network via allowlisted egress and MCP. If both operate on the same workspace or shared mutable resources, concurrent writes and state drift are likely. Because no locking or isolation is documented, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git checkout
IF either agent mutates shared files without an external lock
mitigations: Assign separate working directories immediately
Pause one agent while the other writes shared state
Use a file lock around any shared artifact
Verify no git operations occur in the shared path
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can emit context-rich outputs through MCP, and transformers can act on files, shell, browsers, and subprocesses. That creates a pathway where one agent's output becomes the other's operational input without verification, enabling compounding mistakes or unsafe actions. The pair lacks a documented validation gate, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF transformers uses MemMachine-generated text as authoritative task input
IF transformers executes actions based on unverified MemMachine outputs
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking
Require citations or source links for all MemMachine-derived claims
Limit transformers to drafting only for one run
Log every handoff for review
requires-engineering: add policy checks before shell or browser actions

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while transformers processes text, images, audio, and video with broad file and network surfaces. If regulated or retention-sensitive data flows from MemMachine into transformers, mismatched handling and retention policies can create compliance gaps. The profiles do not document residency or certifications, so the risk is moderate and uncertain.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in MemMachine context
IF transformers persists or transmits that data under a different retention policy
mitigations: Classify the data before any handoff
Exclude regulated records from the pair for one run
Check retention settings on both systems
Document where outputs are stored
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
